name: Minimum regime performance gate
note: Gates a sub-strategy on the worst annualised Sharpe it has ever produced over ANY admissible one-split partition of its own history -- Alexander & Fabozzi's MRP1, a minimax over split points rather than a mean or a rolling window -- recomputed every recheck bars over the trailing history. No new entries while MRP1 is below the floor, and everything is flattened and the strategy retired for three recheck periods whenever MRP1 has deteriorated by more than drop_t against its reading three periods earlier, which is the paper's early-warning signal. The floor and the deterioration trigger are quoted in units of one segment's Sharpe standard error rather than the paper's raw -0.10 and 0.25: on multi-decade daily data one 500-bar segment's Sharpe has a standard error near 0.7, on this study's windows it is near 10, so the raw numbers would be a threshold no real window reaches. The gated rule is the study's own EMA-cross floor family, so what is measured is the gate. Only the s=1 split is computed; s>=2 is quadratic in window length and would dominate the run.
source: Alexander, N. & Fabozzi, F.J., 'Measuring Strategy-Decay Risk: Minimum Regime Performance and the Durability of Systematic Investing', arXiv:2604.08356, Eqs. 3-4 and Exhibits 3-4. Code repository cited by the authors: github.com/nolanalexander/minimum_regime_performance

import math as _m

def _ema(c, n):
    a = 2.0 / (n + 1.0)
    out = [None] * len(c)
    s = None
    for i, x in enumerate(c):
        s = x if s is None else s + a * (x - s)
        if i >= n:
            out[i] = s
    return out

def _bars_per_year(bars):
    """252 sessions of however many bars this symbol actually prints a day."""
    days = set()
    for b in bars:
        days.add(str(b["t"])[:10])
    d = max(1, len(days))
    return (len(bars) / float(d)) * 252.0


def family_init(ctx):
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    bpy = _bars_per_year(bars)
    ann = _m.sqrt(bpy)

    # ---- the sub-strategy being gated: the study's own floor rule, so what
    # ---- is being measured is the gate and not a new signal
    ef = _ema(c, int(ctx.p.base_f))
    es = _ema(c, int(ctx.p.base_s))
    pos = [0] * n
    ev = [0] * n
    for i in range(n):
        if ef[i] is not None and es[i] is not None:
            pos[i] = 1 if ef[i] > es[i] else -1
            if i and pos[i - 1] and pos[i] != pos[i - 1]:
                ev[i] = pos[i]
    ctx.ev = ev

    # its per-bar return series, and prefix sums so any segment's Sharpe is O(1)
    ps = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    pq = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        r = 0.0
        if i and pos[i - 1] and c[i - 1] > 0:
            r = pos[i - 1] * (c[i] / c[i - 1] - 1.0)
        ps[i + 1] = ps[i] + r
        pq[i + 1] = pq[i] + r * r

    def sr(a, b):
        m = b - a
        if m < 30:
            return None
        s1 = ps[b] - ps[a]
        s2 = pq[b] - pq[a]
        mu = s1 / m
        var = (s2 - m * mu * mu) / (m - 1)
        if var <= 0.0:
            return None
        return mu / _m.sqrt(var) * ann

    d = int(ctx.p.min_seg)
    hist = int(ctx.p.hist)
    every = max(1, int(ctx.p.recheck))
    # the floor and the deterioration trigger are quoted in units of one
    # segment's own Sharpe standard error, so they mean the same thing at any
    # bar size: sqrt(bars_per_year / d) annualised Sharpe points
    seg_se = _m.sqrt(bpy / d)
    floor = float(ctx.p.floor_t) * seg_se
    dropby = float(ctx.p.drop_t) * seg_se
    look = int(ctx.p.drop_lag)
    retire_n = int(ctx.p.retire_mult) * every

    elig = [False] * n
    hold = [False] * n          # retired: flatten and take nothing
    seen = []                   # (bar, MRP1) at each recheck
    ok = False
    retired_until = -1
    for t in range(n):
        if t % every == 0:
            lo = max(0, t - hist)
            best = None
            if t - lo >= 2 * d:
                for tau in range(lo + d, t - d + 1):
                    a = sr(lo, tau)
                    b = sr(tau, t)
                    if a is None or b is None:
                        continue
                    v = a if a < b else b
                    if best is None or v < best:
                        best = v
            if best is not None:
                ok = best >= floor
                # a worsening worst regime is the paper's early warning
                if len(seen) >= look:
                    prev = seen[-look]
                    if prev is not None and (prev - best) > dropby:
                        retired_until = t + retire_n
                seen.append(best)
            else:
                ok = False
                seen.append(None)
        hold[t] = t < retired_until
        elig[t] = ok and not hold[t]
    ctx.elig = ctx.series(elig, "eligible")
    ctx.hold = ctx.series(hold, "retired")


def signal(ctx, i):
    if not ctx.elig[i]:
        return 0
    s = ctx.ev[i]
    return 1 if s > 0 else (-1 if s < 0 else 0)


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    return bool(ctx.hold[i])
